title: T-systems: a theory of orthonormal functions with a tridiagonal differentiation matrix
summary: The starting point of this paper is that a spectral method is essentially a combination of an orthonormal basis of the underlying Hilbert space with Galerkin conditions. The choice of an orthonormal basis depends on a number of desirable features which we explore in the context of spectral methods for time-dependent partial differential equations in a single space dimension. A central role in ensuring many of the above features is played by the differentiation matrix of the underlying orthonormal system.
